carousels.name: Exam and deadline stress is a relapse trap

slides.title: Exam week is when your streak [[is most at risk.]]
slides.sub: Stress looks for an exit. Here's how to give it a better one.

slides.title: Stress wants [[relief]]
slides.body: Pressure builds and your brain hunts for the fastest way out. For many people, that has always been the old habit.

slides.title: "Just a [[quick break]]"
slides.body: A break turns into a scroll, a scroll turns into a search. An hour later, you're more stressed and further behind.

slides.title: Plan your [[breaks]]
slides.body: Unplanned breaks are where relapses hide. Decide in advance what a break looks like — and where your phone is.

slides.title: Study-week [[rules]]
slides.note: Students: when is your hardest time to stay clean? 👇

slides.title:
Pass your exams.
[[Keep your streak.]]
slides.lead: Block p*rn completely, track your streak and get instant tools when stress turns into urges.

carousels.name: 3 questions to ask yourself every night

slides.title: 3 questions that will [[change your recovery.]]
slides.sub: Ask them every night for a week. Watch what you start noticing.

slides.title: When did I feel the [[strongest]] urge?
slides.body: Time, place, mood, what you were doing. Patterns show up fast once you write them down.

slides.title: What did I [[need]] in that moment?
slides.body: Rest? Company? A break? Comfort? The urge is often a signal for something else.

slides.title: What will I do [[differently]] tomorrow?
slides.body: One small change. Not a whole new life. Small changes, repeated, are how habits actually break.

slides.title: Why [[writing]] works
slides.body: A thought in your head disappears. A note on paper becomes a pattern you can see. Many people say journaling showed them triggers they'd missed for years.
slides.note: Would you try this for 7 days? Comment "I'm in" 👇

slides.title:
See your patterns.
[[Break your patterns.]]
slides.lead: Daily journaling built for recovery: reflect on urges, spot triggers and build self-awareness.

slides.kicker: Send this to your younger brother
slides.title: What I wish someone told me [[at 15.]]
slides.sub: Nobody talks about this with teenagers. Someone should.

slides.title: It's [[not]] just harmless curiosity
slides.body: What starts as curiosity can quietly turn into a daily habit. Many people say theirs started before they even understood it.

slides.title: You're not [[the only one]]
slides.body: It feels like a secret only you have. It isn't. Millions of guys are dealing with the same thing in silence.

slides.title: Shame won't [[fix]] it
slides.body: Hating yourself doesn't make you stop. It makes you hide. What helps is honesty, tools and support.

slides.title: What [[actually]] helps
items: Keep screens out of the bedroom at night.
Fill your time with sport, friends, skills.
Start early — it's easier at 15 than at 25.

It's never too

slides.lead: A private, shame-free recovery app with guided lessons, a blocker and anonymous support.

slides.title: 4 myths that keep you [[stuck in the loop.]]
slides.sub: Believing #2 is why most people give up.

slides.title: "It's [[just a phase.]]"
slides.body: Phases end on their own. Habits usually don't. If you've been "growing out of it" for years, it might be time to act.

slides.title: "I just need more [[willpower.]]"
slides.body: Willpower runs out. Systems don't. Blockers, routines and support do the heavy lifting when willpower is tired.

slides.title: "One slip [[ruins]] everything."
slides.body: A slip is one moment, not a reset of everything you've learned. What you do in the next hour matters more.

slides.title: "I have to do this [[alone.]]"
slides.body: Doing it alone is the hardest way to do it. An anonymous community or one trusted person changes everything.
slides.note: Which myth did you believe? Comment the number 👇

slides.title:
Drop the myths.
[[Use what works.]]
slides.lead: Systems, not just willpower: a blocker, 1-on-1 accountability and a step-by-step recovery program.

carousels.name: From 'trying to quit' to 'I don't do that'

slides.title: Stop saying "I'm trying to quit." Start saying [["I don't do that."]]
"Trying" leaves the [[door open]]
slides.body: "I'm trying to quit" quietly means "I still do it." Your brain hears a maybe.

slides.title: Identity [[decides]] for you
slides.body: A non-smoker doesn't debate every cigarette. They just don't smoke. The decision is already made.

slides.title: Every day is a [[vote]]
slides.body: Each clean day is a vote for the person you're becoming. You don't need to win every vote — just most of them.

slides.title: Build the [[new you]]
items: Act like him — how does he spend his evenings?
Forgive slips without changing who you are.
slides.note: Type it in the comments: "I don't do that." 👇

slides.title:
Become someone who
[[doesn't need the escape.]]
slides.lead: Streaks, daily journaling and a step-by-step program that turns new habits into who you are.
